state_summary: Seed 6101, free_llm32_dual_expert_v1, round 5: 493 observed records, 2837 declared eligible candidates, no pending records and no validation/test records. Latest measured feedback strengthens graph-dependent solvent-response learning while narrowing the value of further broad loading grids. m205, m28, m200 and m45 reveal substantial prospective response errors; m120 at 1/1 and m82 completion at 20/1 show little loading-associated change. The objective remains overall Row V1/V2 accuracy and label efficiency after retraining.
important_observations:
Nitrogen hypothesis revised: observed 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4 establishes late m211 completion at low-dose 50/1, measuring 26.27/81.78 mL. Against same-dose 20/1 record 434e465cfa7e0034f233, onset decreases by 2.61 mL while completion increases by 34.21 mL. Higher-dose 50/1 record 0f06772820e6693753e3 measures 46.44/103.28: loading displaces both endpoints by about 20–22 mL while physical interval widths remain similar, 55.51 versus 56.84 mL. High loading therefore does not explain away the broad interval. Fixed-dose m90 measures 14.42/29.27, 30.71/60.60 and 48.17/107.99 at 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 in 0460dfc4e1747f0fc92c, 855832bd4005ac7abdc6 and 96710afeabc594baa359. Historical V2 error changes from +6.07 to -25.19 mL across that range; a shared nitrogen correction remains unsupported.

Hydroxyl loading hypothesis narrowed: m120 records 2bd6619109218dcf6580 and 880646809d9f015053f6 measure 10.54/16.67 and 10.62/17.23 at 1/1 and 55.65 versus 166.95 mg. The large earlier-elution shift does not persist there. At 2/1 those doses measure 19.89/29.02 and 8.03/10.83 in 4ee22742c686bdbb1cb9 and a5f9f0327623c4752e2e. The recorded solvent response therefore changes direction with dose. Correction to prior memory: the higher-loading 5/1 record e4fd83fb3852eb354a66 uses 111.3 mg, not 166.95 mg. Only the 1/1 and 2/1 comparisons complete the identical two-dose design. These records support an interaction question without establishing saturation, dissolution or another mechanism.

Hydroxyl transfer remains incomplete: matched m119 rises from 11.83/19.31 to 48.00/77.09 across 1/1 to 5/1 in 25ffcaa2164643e082b9 and 776ee2c1e85ebde75168. Matched low-dose m205 rises from 10.51/25.36 to 54.52/89.72 in b1fcf9bf2e03028d2ef8 and 7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2, rejecting its predicted retention decrease. m200 rises from 15.15/37.40 at 1/1 to 33.88/74.44 at 2/1 in 97318de99bab4460cf4e and a92f7617b135de150588. Historical V2 underpredictions reach 59.05 mL for m205 and 42.81 for m200. The inference is that graph-dependent transition locations matter; m120's dose behavior should not be transferred universally.

Beta-ketoester loading control largely resolved: m82 records 61090cfdcf019e0891a3 and b6bf451b4911ee22d4a4 measure 26.33/64.40 and 24.23/64.37 at 20/1 and 102.9 versus 154.35 mg. Completion barely differs descriptively, while onset moves earlier by 2.10 mL. m94 also has relatively stable completion across tested 20/1 doses but a larger onset change. This weakens the need for another extensive family loading grid; it does not establish statistical equivalence or a universal dose law.

Ordinary response hypothesis refined: matched m68 completion follows 12.58, 25.62, 19.59 and 17.50 mL across 2/1, 5/1, 10/1 and 20/1, with onset near 5–6 mL. New records e3716bf7dba67a0f2185 and f1e08c239f1c0950ad36 support the recorded local completion maximum, without establishing same-input reproducibility. m27 follow-ups 59d8c3d932aece6945ae and f5e5ad6e9b48aa9731b5 are accurate, reducing continuation value after its earlier extreme overprediction. New transfer remains heterogeneous: m28 record 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a has V2 underprediction of 57.87 mL; m164 record b7fffd840d208b29776c has 18.30 mL underprediction; m201 record d6faa7e77464f5f9a34b has 9.05 mL overprediction.

Acid/ester hypothesis gains measured support: fixed-setup m45 rises from 6.63/9.00 to 39.58/65.65 across 1/1 to 20/1 in 5e2f71c50a4ccaa1b83e and b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1. m46 changes only from 5.66/7.83 to 6.29/10.44 in 84a50941febef9dc2c8f and ad98d4ead60516eb3972. Their within-molecule slopes differ substantially. Different masses and graphs prevent assigning the entire contrast causally to esterification.
candidate_scientific_questions: Prospective questions with remaining value include locating the solvent-response transition on m119, m45 and m164; distinguishing persistence across loading from a dose interaction for the m28 tail; and testing transfer to unmeasured ordinary ester, fused ketone and biphenyl-aldehyde graphs. A modest prediction or narrow quantile width can still distinguish competing explanations. These questions are alternatives whose marginal value depends on the other experiments considered, rather than a proposed batch.
possible_model_blind_spots: Inference from this trajectory: corrections learned on acquired graphs do not reliably transfer across nitrogen topology, hydroxyl connectivity or solvent ratio. Shared functionality is insufficient to determine residual direction. Model diagnostics also suggest weak conditional use of loading features. Chemical explanations remain hypotheses. As an ML prior, matched interior anchors can distinguish response curvature more efficiently than repeatedly extending extreme endpoints.
important_model_behaviors:
Current prediction diagnostic: loading sensitivity remains nearly absent in many dose triplets. At m28 10/1, db7f9ffa50eb931613f6 and 0dccaa29989ef4956786 span 58.4–175.2 mg but predict approximately 38.08/79.28 and 38.08/79.29 mL. Similar flatness occurs on m119, m205 and m92. Flat predictions are appropriate for some measured contrasts, including m120 at 1/1 and m82 V2 at 20/1; the concern is failure to express sensitivity conditionally.

Current quantile diagnostic: m76 f106b85660c480a44538 has V1 q90 below its median despite a positive reported width. m48 adbaa4b00d492d64eed5 has negative V1 quantile width. m28 686562279e2bfb73ef1e has q10 above its median. Width rankings cannot be interpreted as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

Inference: separate onset and completion information is essential. m211 broadening, m68's completion maximum and the beta-ketoester loading contrasts distinguish interval changes from common endpoint displacement. Current adaptation toward acquired m28 or m200 labels is a fit diagnostic, not evidence of prospective transfer.
possible_learning_bottlenecks: Condition scaling or interaction capacity may limit returns from additional loading labels. Existing contrasts already require graph-by-ratio-by-loading responses. Sparse matched ratio anchors leave transition locations unidentified, making an interior measurement potentially valuable. Adaptive acquisition concentrates residual evidence on recent failures and cannot estimate target-distribution weights or overall Row error. Local variation and omitted experimental factors may also limit learning; replication is useful when its outcome would change interpretation or training influence.
coverage_or_redundancy_concerns:
Assess redundancy using molecule plus all five condition columns. Identical inputs occur under multiple eligible IDs, such as m76 f106b85660c480a44538 and 62c643c64fefa1a9b0c1. Candidate 07a55cdab65b05f31561 repeats an observed m82 physical input; another label would be replication. Tiny mass differences do not automatically add useful coverage.

The supplied pool offers unmeasured graphs including m16, m38, m76, m149, m157, m189 and m202. Ordinary ester and carbonyl connectivity can complement recent late polar acquisitions. Heavy-halogen graphs overlap substantially with represented chemistry. The formally charged phosphorus graph m202 is structurally distant, but distance alone does not establish transferable value. Further broad m73, m80, m124, m173 or m194 programs have diminished immediate value after prior hypothesis revisions. Recurrence of m194 broad completion across distinct conditions does not establish same-input reproducibility.

warnings: Only observed-table records establish measured evidence; all candidate endpoints remain predictions, including candidates sharing observed physical inputs. Historical errors are prediction minus measurement before acquisition and retraining. Adaptive residuals do not establish unbiased Row accuracy or retraining improvement. V2 minus V1 is physical elution interval width, distinct from predictive quantile width. m3 contains no carbonyl and cannot support a carbonyl-specific explanation. Preserve the conflicting m73 records and the slightly reversed measured m195 interval without silently correcting labels. All conclusions use only this seed and method's supplied trajectory.
